summary: This article explains how tiny living things called microbes help people digest food, make bread and yogurt, enrich the soil, and fight disease.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “Helpful Microbes” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: a tool that makes very small things look much bigger
to break down food in the body so it can be used

challengeTerms.def: a living thing so small it can only be seen with a microscope
a process in which microbes change sugars into other things, such as gas or acid
a gas that makes up most of the air; plants need it in a form they can absorb

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that most germs and microbes are bad for people? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how microbes help both people and plants.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review microscope, harmless, and digest, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use microorganism, fermentation, and nitrogen in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
